subject: If I call a reactive from a observeevent block, will reactive reevaluate the whole reactive block?

messages.author: 11176baa4d39080f
messages.subject: If I call a reactive from a observeevent block, will reactive reevaluate the whole reactive block?
parts:
Hi Guys,

If I call a reactive from an observeEvent code block, will reactive reevaluate the whole reactive block or just use the previous cached values.

For example:

mydate<-reactive({
invalidelater(50000, session)
get my date from mysql db
})

observeEvent(input$button,{
output$text<-renderText("textID", mydata())
}

so if I click the button, will mydata() be re-evaluated from the server or just used previously calculated value?

it is important :-)

someone can help me understand this question

many thanks,
Yi

messages.author: 5bbc8524a66e9988
messages.subject: Re: If I call a reactive from a observeevent block, will reactive reevaluate the whole reactive block?
parts:
It is supposed to use the latest value, it won't be revaluated.
mydata() depends on what's written inside the reactive expression or any reactive values inside it. 

And if you'd like to see exactly when mydata() changes, you could use a simple `print("here)` inside the reactive expression and see on the console when it gets evaluated.

 mydate <- reactive({
     print("here")
     invalidelater(50000, session)
     ## get my date from mysql db
   })


One more thing, you can render the text directly without `observeEvent`, but use `isolate()` to make the rendering only dependent on the button. So here it will be as if you say "Once you click the button, take the current value of myData() and render text"

output$text <- renderText({
   input$button
   isolate(myData())
  })
